The checkout does not bear that theory out. Task 1 (asf/improve/measure.py, classes.py, the 439-line tests/test_improve.py) is already landed and its 52 tests pass clean, so Task 2 alone is a small, ready, self-contained unit with no drift against its own anchors (approvals.py, cli.py, record/new.py). Task 3's half is not ready: asf/tick/steps.py's STEPS manifest has grown from the 5 steps the plan assumes to the 9 it carries today (record, health, groom, wave, prs, harvest, batch, watchdog, daily), a daily-catch-up mechanism (B-0123) was added after the plan was written, and every line anchor the plan cites for Task 3 (steps.py:24-35/:137-160; tick.py:292-294/:313-314/:404) now points at unrelated code — confirmed directly against asf/tick/tick.py and asf/tick/steps.py in this checkout. Folding a ready 8-file task behind a drifted, heavier one, gated by three large test modules (test_approvals.py 1254 lines, test_tick.py 1150 lines, test_tick_steps.py 1854 lines), produced a unit three CODE sessions in a row could not land a single commit against: worker/T-0073 still sits exactly at origin/main. Upheld: the merge is overruled on the checkout's evidence, not on the overlap theory that motivated it; T-0073 reverts to Task 2's own scope via the writes: field below (no tracked file in this repo carries the footprint — it lives on the card the groom merge touched, so the field is the whole edit). T-0074 is no longer delivered by T-0073: it must be reopened as its own Task, its anchors refreshed against the current asf/tick/steps.py and asf/tick/tick.py, and run after T-0073 lands (Task 3 imports Task 2's cmd_improve). This finding does not come back in a later round.
